requirements.title: Preconnection connects a unit to a file at program start
requirements.definition: Preconnection means that the unit is connected to a file at the beginning of execution of the program.
requirements.oracle:
Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish a non-default state first (for example by writing known records, initializing variables to nonzero/nonblank sentinels, or creating a known file) and then observe only portable properties: exact internal records, successful IOSTAT zero, nonzero IOSTAT for a specified error condition, or named intrinsic status values where the standard names them. Processor-dependent unit numbers, file names, record lengths, storage-unit encodings, buffering, timing, IOMSG text, and specific error numbers are not asserted.

I/O OPEN fixture implementation: 1 valid run-phase program(s) and 0 diagnostic program(s) cover `preconnection-at-program-beginning`. Runtime oracles use controlled stdout/stderr, per-run relative files, INQUIRE properties, exact integer/character/logical values, and only zero/nonzero IOSTAT distinctions. Diagnostics are line-anchored for numbered syntax or constraints and have one-property controls. No IOMSG text, processor-dependent unit number, physical filename, or specific nonzero status is asserted.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Runtime fixture coverage is finite and does not imply fixture review. This packet creates no Fortran fixture, compiler invocation, execution evidence, evidence link, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim. Negative plans are source-control plans unless this unit itself requires rejection and a future fixture can observe the rejection portably. IOMSG wording and processor-dependent numeric status values are never an oracle.
requirements.dependencies: Registered dependencies: clauses 6, 8, 9, 10, and 11 for source form, names, expressions, execution constructs, and existing declaration/execution foundations. Unregistered dependencies explicitly retained: later clause 12 connection, specifier, file-position, data-transfer, internal-file, and input/output-item rules; clause 13 formatting; clause 15 defined I/O; clause 16 inquiry intrinsics where future fixtures need them; clauses 3, 5, 14, 17, 18, and 19 where terminology, constants, images, IEEE support, deleted features, or scope/lifetime controls are reached.

requirements.title: A preconnected unit may be used in I/O statements without a prior OPEN
